judgment.status_reasoning: After the Commerce Committee's substitute (c3, 16 Apr 2025) the bill went to the House Second Reading Calendar, was temporarily postponed on 23 Apr 2025, indefinitely postponed and withdrawn on 3 May 2025, and died on the Second Reading Calendar on 16 Jun 2025 (last action on the bill page). It never passed either chamber; 'Proposed' with status 'Lapsed' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific bill on provenance data for content made with generative AI; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the filing date, 4 Feb 2025; date_last_updated is the posting of c3, the last version, on 16 Apr 2025.
judgment.summary_reasoning: The c3 text, stored for this run, supports every claim of the current summary: generative AI developers (an organization that develops a publicly available generative AI tool), the choice between a provenance application tool for content made with the developer's tool and applying provenance data where technically feasible, the free provenance reader, provenance data compliant with widely adopted standards that shows synthetic (visual) content and names the developer without personally identifying information, the social media platforms' duty, and enforcement only by the Attorney General after a 30-day cure period. Left unchanged.
